experiment_data.hypothesis: A GPU-vectorized DGP grid that systematically varies subgroup misclassification heterogeneity and CATE heterogeneity will reproduce the EC-HTE bias-bound mechanism: positive correlation between error and treatment effect should make global correction worse than uncorrected annotations, while negative correlation should not show the same degradation.

spec.hypothesis: Positive misclassification-CATE correlation makes pooled global confusion correction structurally worse than uncorrected subgroup estimates; negative-correlation controls should show materially lower oracle-global-worse rate.
spec.command: cd /home/root/ec_hte && source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python repro/exp_002_gpu_dgp_grid/run_gpu_dgp_grid.py --config configs/exp_002_gpu_dgp_grid.json --output-dir artifacts/exp_002_gpu_dgp_grid/formal --device cuda
spec.data_path: synthetic DGP generated in-run; outputs under /home/root/ec_hte/artifacts/exp_002_gpu_dgp_grid/formal

environment.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

spec.disk_estimate: <250 MB JSONL/JSON artifacts; no model checkpoint download

operational_criteria.success_rule: Positive-correlation conditions oracle-global-worse rate at least 20 percentage points higher than negative-correlation controls, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0; bias-bound Spearman rho >= 0.50, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0.
